evals.prompt: Use $create-learning-course to create a self-contained introductory Python data-validation course for analysts. Assume basic Python but no validation terminology. Include two lessons, one runnable standard-library lab, a process diagram and official references. Work only in a new local course folder; do not install or publish.
evals.expected_output: A complete light HTML textbook and canonical sources teaching validation before its applications, with a reproducible lab and honest evidence gates.
assertions: The opening explains validation, input/output and failure handling before APIs or applications.
The syllabus and TOC follow the same two-lesson prerequisite sequence.
The lab has a purpose introduction and seven substantive sections whose commands and results match source.
The page embeds full prose, CSS, contextual accessible SVG and complete escaped lab source; the course builder has a stale/parity check.
No GPU, Slurm, cloud, private identifiers or unrequested installation is introduced.
Every lesson title names a concept or relationship rather than listing technologies; syllabus, TOC and body titles match.
Every lesson uses Objective, How it works, Practice and Mental model in that order, followed only by optional References; no lesson-local Glossary or Where to Go Next is created.

How it works defines each needed concept and unfamiliar abbreviation before relying on it, connects the causal steps and includes a concrete worked example; common audience vocabulary is not mechanically expanded.
Each How it works includes its own meaningful diagram with connectors, caption and adjacent explanation that agree; a diagram elsewhere does not satisfy the lesson.
Mental model closes teaching by synthesizing already-taught concepts without introducing a new prerequisite, term or mechanism.

When full-course browser verification is permitted and available, use owned headless Playwright Test with Chrome and isolated state, preserving desktop, 390px and 320px coverage plus keyboard, zoom/reflow, mobile TOC, local scroller and diagram checks.

Browser evidence names the inspected artifact, actual browser/version, headless mode, viewports, assertions, screenshots/traces, visual findings and cleanup after success or failure; optional headless isolated MCP exploration remains separate from repeatable acceptance.

If browser execution is unavailable or denied, continue permitted authoring with the required browser gate pending; do not require screen unlock, foreground windows or monitor selection, bypass a denial, install dependencies without authority, or claim publication readiness.

Each complete course has exactly one shared Glossary after its single Where to Go Next and before final Official references. Collect all taught terms and abbreviations with concise definitions and full expansions where applicable, merge duplicates without losing distinct meanings, and sort unique displayed keys A-Z ignoring case. No lesson or guide has its own glossary.

Each complete course has exactly one Where to Go Next shared by all lessons and guides, before its single Glossary. Concrete bulleted options relate to completed competencies and introduce no required prerequisites, installations, dependencies or completion gates.

Uses shared typography, numbered Official references, bulleted Where to Go Next options and an independent course Glossary; omits visible Course mission and Syllabus while preserving unique learner context in orientation or owning lessons.

evals.prompt: Use $create-learning-course to draft two complete lessons for beginners on managing a waiting line in a small workshop. Lesson one should explain how arrivals, waiting work, service and departures relate. Lesson two should explain first-in, first-out (FIFO) service and work in progress (WIP), comparing a steady arrival rate of two jobs per minute with service capacity of three jobs per minute and showing what changes when arrivals reach four per minute. Assume learners know ordinary arithmetic but no queue terminology. Deliver lesson-only Markdown with original inline SVG diagrams and a short guided non-code exercise with feedback for each lesson; do not create a full course package or use external services. All examples are synthetic. Follow the selected skill's lesson format.
evals.expected_output: Two complete subject-neutral lesson drafts with clear causal teaching, local terminology and meaningful diagrams, preserving lesson-only scope.
assertions: Every lesson title names a concept or relationship rather than listing technologies; no unrequested syllabus or TOC is added for this lesson-only scope.
Every lesson uses Objective, How it works, Practice and Mental model in that order, followed only by optional References; no lesson-local Glossary or Where to Go Next is created.

How it works defines each needed concept and unfamiliar abbreviation before relying on it, connects the causal steps and includes a concrete worked example; common audience vocabulary is not mechanically expanded.
Each How it works includes its own meaningful diagram with connectors, caption and adjacent explanation that agree; a diagram elsewhere does not satisfy the lesson.
Mental model closes teaching by synthesizing already-taught concepts without introducing a new prerequisite, term or mechanism.
FIFO and WIP are expanded and explained in the lesson that uses them; waiting work is distinguished from all unfinished work.
The numerical example distinguishes actual departures from service capacity and explains backlog growth of one job per minute when arrivals exceed capacity.
Practice includes guided non-code work and reasoned feedback; no files, dependencies, full course package or external services are required.
The browser default adds no implicit browser execution, dependency installation, publication or live-lab work to this restricted request.

FIFO and WIP have correct expansions and definitions in the lesson before the Mental model uses them; a standalone lesson has no Glossary or Where to Go Next section, and puts any onward suggestion in the handoff. If an owning course is supplied, update its shared appendices without creating local copies.
